newsitem.title: FRANCE: SIA to add 4th 747 Paris-Singapore freight.
newsitem.headline: SIA to add 4th 747 Paris-Singapore freight.

text.p: Singapore Airlines (SIA) said it plans a fourth scheduled weekly Boeing 747-200 freighter flight between Paris-Charles de Gaulle to Singapore, from end-March 1997.
The existing three flights are operated in conjunction with Air France.
"The additional frequency will be operated by an SIA aircraft and capacity will be shared between ourselves and Air France," a London-based SIA cargo official told Reuters.

The official added: "A fourth weekly freighter flight was introduced on ad hoc basis last autumn and we have now decided to upgrade it to a scheduled frequency as a result of strong demand forecast for 1997."

In December 1996, air cargo exports on the Paris-Singapore route totalled 1,090 tonnes, up 70.6 percent on December 1995, the highest growth rate of all the major ex-Paris freight traffic routes in the month in question, Paris airport authority figures show.
For all of 1996 air cargo exports on the Paris-Singapore route totalled 9,054 tonnes, an increase of 20.5 percent on 1995.
The additional flight means SIA and Air France aircraft will each operate two of the four weekly freighter frequencies on the Paris-Singapore route.

"From June 1 1997, SIA plans to replace its two 200Fs on the route with 747-400 "Mega Ark" freighters offering 10 to 20 tonnes extra capacity per flight as a result of an extra main deck position," the official added.

SIA also carries freight on a daily, non-stop Airbus 340-300 passenger service between Paris and Singapore able to carry around 11 tonnes of cargo per flight. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax +5017
